questions.question: If two cars travel the exact same distance of 100 meters, how does the speed of the faster car affect its travel time?
options: It takes more time to cover the distance.
It takes a shorter time to cover the distance.
The travel time remains exactly the same.
It takes double the time of the slower car.

questions.question: Which of the following formulas is used to calculate the speed of an object?
options: Speed = distance + time
Speed = distance × time
Speed = distance ÷ time
Speed = time ÷ distance

questions.question: Which of the following is a standard unit used to measure speed?
options: Metres per second (m/s)
Kilograms per metre (kg/m)
Newtons per second (N/s)
Seconds per metre (s/m)

questions.question: What is the direct effect of a non-zero resultant force acting on a moving object?
options: It always keeps the speed completely constant.
It can change the speed of the object.
It immediately stops the object from moving.
It makes the mass of the object increase.

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line (greater gradient) represent?
options: The object has stopped moving.
The object is moving at a slower speed.
The object is moving at a faster speed.
The object is moving backwards.

questions.question: When does a falling object reach its terminal velocity in the air?
options: When the drag force becomes much greater than the gravitational force.
When the drag force and gravitational force are equal.
When there is no drag force acting on the object.
When gravity stops pulling the object downwards.

questions.question: How does increasing the surface area of a parachute affect its air resistance?
options: It makes the drag force bigger.
It makes the drag force smaller.
It has no effect on the drag force.
It reduces the drag force to zero.

questions.question: When a skydiver is falling at top speed with a parachute, how does the drag force compare to the force of gravity on the jumper?
options: The drag force is larger than the force of gravity.
The drag force is smaller than the force of gravity.
The drag force is the same size as the force of gravity.
The drag force is zero.

questions.question: What does a completely horizontal, level line on a distance-time graph represent?
options: An object moving at a constant, high speed
An object that is accelerating rapidly
A stationary object with no movement
An object returning to its starting position

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what is indicated by an upward sloping line and a downward sloping line?
options: Movement in opposite directions
Acceleration followed by deceleration
Movement at the exact same constant speed
No movement in either case

questions.question: To ensure an accurate measurement when observing an event, where should the observer stand?
options: At a 45-degree angle to the observation point
Directly in line with the observation
As far away from the finish line as possible
Slightly behind the starting line facing away

questions.question: Why do scientists take repeat readings during an experiment?
options: To increase the size of the systematic error
To reduce the effect of random errors
To make the experiment take longer
To guarantee that all readings are exactly identical

questions.question: In which direction does friction always act on a moving object?
options: In the same direction as the object's movement
Against the direction of movement of the object
Perpendicular to the direction of movement
Directly downwards towards the center of the Earth

questions.question: According to the laws of motion, what will happen to an object moving at a steady speed in a straight line if no resultant force acts on it?
options: It will gradually slow down and come to a stop.
It will continue to move at a steady speed in a straight line.
It will immediately speed up.
It will change its direction of movement randomly.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of streamlining the design of a high-speed vehicle?
options: It increases the weight of the vehicle.
It reduces the drag force acting on it.
It eliminates gravitational pull entirely.
It decreases the vehicle's engine power.
